name: Combination Skin
description: Combination skin refers to a condition where the skin is oily in some areas and dry in others. Typically, the T-zone (forehead, nose, chin) tends to be oilier while the cheeks may appear drier.

morning_routine.purpose: Gently remove any overnight oils and impurities without stripping the skin.

night_routine.action: Cleanse with a gentle, balancing cleanser
night_routine.purpose: Remove daily grime and excess oil while maintaining hydration in dry areas.

night_routine.action: Apply a lightweight hydrating serum or moisturizer focused on the T-zone
night_routine.purpose: Targeted moisture application to prevent overhydration and breakouts.

night_routine.action: Moisturize the cheeks with a richer cream
night_routine.purpose: Provide extra hydration where needed without exacerbating oiliness.

weekly_care: Exfoliate once or twice per week using a gentle, chemical exfoliant to prevent congestion and maintain even skin tone.
common_mistakes: Using heavy products that can clog pores in the T-zone
Neglecting dry areas, leading to a patchy texture
do: Choose multi-purpose skincare products whenever possible
dont: Over-exfoliate which can irritate combination skin and worsen oil production in the T-zone
Skip moisturization, even on oily areas; it helps maintain barrier function

seasonal_care.summer: Focus on lighter, cooling ingredients like aloe vera to soothe excess oils and protect from sun damage.
seasonal_care.winter: Use richer, hydrating products to combat dryness without adding excess oil. Avoid overly hot showers that can strip natural oils.

expert_tips: Regularly assess and adjust your skincare routine to match the changing needs of combination skin throughout the seasons.
